payload.claim: Every new test that checks whether `witness` is advisory or blocking (this one, plus the two modified assertions at lines ~1793 and ~1970) sets the tier via `_spec(risk=tier, ...)` directly, never via an `elevate_on` path match. In `saffron/cell/session.py:987`, the blocking decision is `witness_blocking(cast(RiskTier, current_tier))`, where `current_tier` is `effective_risk(spec.risk, changed, policy.elevate_on)` — the same variable the `size` advisory check above it (line 978) already uses. Swapping that one occurrence to `spec.risk` (leaving `size`'s check untouched) would make `witness` ignore an `elevate_on`-triggered elevation, and no test in this diff or the existing suite would fail: `test_an_elevate_on_match_elevates_a_standard_spec_for_the_suite` (test_session.py:1919) exercises exactly that elevation path but never inspects `advisory_gates`, and none of the witness-specific tests use `elevate_on` to diverge `current_tier` from `spec.risk`.
